verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes' warrant sources by retrieval (doc.rust-lang.org book/reference/error-code pages, rustc-dev-guide, RFCs, rust-lang/rust and rust-clippy source for two pages that truncated on fetch, two blog posts, two docs.rs pages pinned at rapier3d-f64 0.35.3, and the ICSE 2022 Rust-challenges PDF via pdftotext), verified all 6 engine_note claims against solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs and solver/Cargo.toml (all accurate), and ran 7 of the recipes' own check snippets through compile_oracle.py myself on the pinned 1.98.1 toolchain to settle the highest-uncertainty claims (all matched exactly, including two edge cases central to whole recipes: From::from not reborrowing, and NLL problem-case-3/Polonius examples). Two defects found. Systemic weakness: two recipes (two-phase borrows; disjoint closure capture) cite a pre-2021 RFC (2025; 2229) as the SOLE documentary warrant for one specific, still-load-bearing edge case (indexing forces immediate borrow activation / counts as an impure capture) that their companion current source (rustc-dev-guide; the 2021 Edition Guide) covers only in general and silently omits — recency compliance for that detail depended on nobody having re-checked it against the live compiler, which I did (both still hold on 1.98.1). One factual defect: recipe 9's ICSE-paper source claim cites "finding 6" for the array-vs-tuple participant-confusion result; the paper's own text says "explaining Finding 5 in Section 3.3" — Finding 6 is a different, unrelated finding about compiler-message completeness.
